messages.content: You are a helpful assistant experienced in law-firm operations and legal practice management, helping the partners of a small boutique firm plan a strategic expansion.

Hi, so Okafor & Vance is finally big enough that we're planning a real expansion, a new practice area, a second office, some lateral hires, the whole thing, over the next quarter. I'd like to use you as a planning partner across all of it. Sound good?
Sounds good — happy to be your planning partner across the whole expansion. Let's take it piece by piece, starting wherever you'd like.

Let's start with the practice-area question since it drives everything else. We're an IP-and-startup boutique thinking about adding a formal employment-law practice. What should we be weighing before we commit to standing up a whole new group?

Weigh demand and referral pipeline, staffing and conflicts risk against existing IP clients, upfront investment versus billable ramp-up time, and whether a lateral hire or ground-up build makes more sense before committing.
On the office side, we're deciding between a full second office downtown or just taking an extra floor in our current building. What's the general tradeoff for a firm our size?
A full second office signals commitment but costs more upfront in buildout and lease term; an extra floor is cheaper and faster but may cap your growth and blur the two practices together.

Quick clarification: when I say 'the practice' to you, I always mean the new employment-law group we're standing up, not the firm as a whole, even though people here casually call the whole firm 'the practice' too. Just the new group, when I say it to you.
Understood, I'll keep that scoped correctly going forward.
For lateral hires, is it smarter to recruit one senior partner with a book of business or two mid-level associates who are cheaper but bring no clients?
A senior partner with a book de-risks revenue faster but costs more in comp and integration friction; two associates are cheaper but you're betting on organic growth.

Office decision time. We looked at three routes: (1) take a full second office downtown, (2) just lease an extra floor in our current building, or (3) a hybrid where we keep our current floor and add a small satellite suite near the courthouse for litigation staff. After running the numbers with our accountant, we're going with the hybrid, current floor plus the small courthouse satellite.
That's a sensible way to balance cost and litigation convenience — good call.
Malpractice insurance renews in ninety days. Does adding an employment-law practice usually spike the premium a lot?
Yes, adding a new litigation-adjacent practice area almost always bumps the premium, sometimes meaningfully, so get quotes early rather than after you've committed headcount.

Hard preference on the employment practice: absolutely no contingency-fee plaintiff-side cases. I think they'd conflict with our management-side corporate clients and blow up our reputation with the exact companies we serve. I don't care how lucrative a big case looks, we are not taking contingency plaintiff work, ever.
Understood, I'll keep that boundary in mind for everything we plan around the new group.

Also, when I say 'the vault' from now on, I mean the physical secured file room where we keep original signed client documents, not the encrypted digital document archive, which some of the associates also call 'the vault.' Two different things, and I only mean the physical room.
Got it, noted the distinction.
On case management, our current system is creaking. What features matter most when a boutique firm shops for a new platform?
Conflict checking, document assembly, and calendaring/deadline tracking tend to matter most for a boutique firm, more than flashy reporting dashboards.

For context, we tried a case-management platform called CaseHelm for about eight months two years ago. It corrupted a document index twice and their support took a week to respond both times. We ripped it out and will never use CaseHelm again.
Noted, I'll steer clear of that option in anything I suggest.

On laterals, we had three candidates on the table: (1) Marisol Reyes, a senior partner with a large employment book, (2) two mid-level associates from a regional firm with no portable clients, or (3) a semi-retired judge willing to come on of counsel part-time. We talked it through and we're going with Marisol Reyes, the senior partner with the book.
Makes sense given the book of business she brings.
Back to the employment practice, how many attorneys do we realistically need on day one to service it credibly?
Realistically two to three attorneys, at least one senior enough to originate and supervise, so you're not fielding client matters solo on day one.
Random note for the file: the courthouse satellite suite base rent is $6,400 a month before any escalation. Just logging that, doesn't change what we're discussing.
Logged, thanks for the note.

One more firm rule: no billing our startup clients in six-minute increments for quick emails and calls. We did nickel-and-dime billing at my old firm and it torched client relationships. Flat monthly retainers for the startup clients only, even if we technically leave money on the table.
Got it, noted — that'll shape how we structure engagement letters for those clients.
For the lease, the landlord wants a ten-year term with a personal guaranty from the partners. Is a personal guaranty a normal ask?
It's common, especially for a firm without a long financial track record, but you can often negotiate it down to a declining guaranty over the lease term.
Let's just codename the whole employment-practice launch 'Elantris' from here on, in every planning doc and email, so we're not spelling it out every time.
Works for me — I'll use that name going forward.

Also, remember we used a legal-recruiting agency called Bright & Marlow for our last two searches and both placements left within a year, plus they double-billed us on a fee once. We dropped them and aren't going back.
Understood, that vendor's off the table.
On recruiting, what's a reasonable timeline to land a quality lateral partner from first conversation to start date?
Three to six months is typical from serious first conversation to start date once you factor in notice periods and diligence on the book of business.
For the record, our malpractice renewal quote came in under policy number MAL-2026-77413, with the binder due back by March 9th. Just logging it.
Got it, thanks for flagging.
For insurance, should we increase our per-claim limit before or after we take on the new practice area?
I'd increase the limit before you take on the new practice, since retroactive coverage gaps are painful and insurers price prospective risk more predictably.
Let's codename the case-management software migration 'Scadrial', since it's the messiest, most behind-schedule part of the whole expansion. Use that name for it in any status update.
Sounds good, I'll refer to it that way in updates.
On technology, how important is it that the new case-management system integrates with our existing document-management setup?
Fairly important — re-keying documents between two systems creates exactly the kind of friction and error risk a growing firm can't absorb.
For the buildout, how much should we budget for conference-room and privacy improvements in a legal office specifically?
Budget generously for sound-isolated conference rooms and at least one private call room; privacy is a differentiator for both IP and employment clients.
One more on recruiting: should we use a legal-recruiting firm or try to source laterals through our own network first?
Start with your own network for speed and lower cost, and only bring in a recruiting firm if that search stalls after six to eight weeks.
Does the practice need its own separate intake process before we open the second office?
Yes, I'd stand up a lightweight standalone intake so new matters get properly conflict-checked before they mix with existing files.
How much shelving capacity do we need in the vault after we merge the two client bases?
Plan for growth room beyond the current volume — enough shelving to comfortably hold both client bases plus a buffer for a few years.
On the office decision, no need to walk through it again, but what signage do we need to order for it?
Order directional signage for the satellite entrance and a small lobby placard; keep the primary office signage as-is.
For the lateral we picked, don't re-explain who it is, just tell me what the standard onboarding conflict check involves.
It's a standard cross-check against her prior clients and matters for conflicts before she can open a new file with you.
What's still open on the Elantris punch list before we can announce the new group?
Mainly finalizing the practice group's engagement-letter templates and locking the malpractice endorsement — both are close but not signed off yet.
Any movement on Scadrial this week, or is it still stalled?
Still stalled — the vendor's data-migration step hasn't cleared, so no real movement since last week.
For the lease, besides term length and the guaranty, what else should I be scrutinizing before we sign?
Scrutinize the escalation clause, exclusivity/non-compete language, and your termination and subletting rights before signing.
